about.title: San Bernardino Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A space heater that ignites, a ladder rung that gives way, a car seat that fails on I-215 during a Friday evening commute. Defective products reach San Bernardino homes and workplaces every day, and the people hurt by them often assume the fault must somehow be their own. Under California law, that is rarely the question. Product liability claims here generally run on strict liability, meaning you need to show the item had a design, manufacturing, or warning defect and that the defect caused your injury. Whether the maker was negligent is usually beside the point. This matters in a county the size of San Bernardino County, where goods move through in enormous volume before landing on store shelves along E Highland Avenue or W Baseline Street. The manufacturer, the distributor, and the retailer can each be held responsible. What tends to decide these cases is evidence, and the most important piece of evidence is the product itself. LawProactive is a free service that connects San Bernardino residents with an independent attorney who works on contingency, so there is no fee unless you recover.

items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers may all share liability under California law. The attorney you are connected with can look at the entire chain rather than stopping at the store where you bought it.

items.question: My airbag did not deploy in a collision on SR-210. Is that a product liability case or a car accident case?
items.answer: It may be both. San Bernardino recorded 1,380 injury collisions in 2025, and some of those injuries are made worse by a vehicle component that fails to work as designed. If an airbag, seatbelt, or tire defect contributed to your harm, a claim against the manufacturer can proceed alongside any claim against another driver. Keep the vehicle from being scrapped or repaired until an attorney has had a chance to review it.

items.question: Do I have to prove the company was careless to win a product liability claim in California?
items.answer: Generally, no. California applies strict liability to most defective product claims, so the focus is on whether the product had a defect and whether that defect caused your injury. How careful the manufacturer was is usually not the deciding issue. That said, gathering proof of the defect still takes work, which is where an attorney comes in.

items.question: I already threw away the box and the receipt. Can I still pursue a claim?
items.answer: Possibly, but the product itself matters most, so hold on to it in its current condition and do not attempt repairs. Photos of the item, the injury, and the scene help, and bank or card statements can often stand in for a lost receipt. An attorney connected through LawProactive can advise on what else to collect and whether purchase records can be traced through the San Bernardino retailer.
